title: Lilly and Norwegian Cruise Beat Before the Bell as DoorDash Agrees to Buy Instacart
dek: Eli Lilly and Norwegian Cruise Line topped estimates for the third quarter, while DoorDash's $17 billion deal for Instacart and the 8:30 AM GDP release set the morning's agenda.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The Federal Reserve Building in Washington, D.C.

keyPoints: Eli Lilly reported adjusted EPS of $7.48 against a $6.26 consensus per LSEG, and revenue of $24.4 billion against $22.61 billion expected; shares rose about 4.5% premarket.
Norwegian Cruise Line reported adjusted EPS of $1.12 versus 93 cents expected per FactSet and revenue of $2.95 billion versus $2.88 billion; shares jumped about 13%.

DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart's parent Maplebear for $65 a share in cash and stock, an 11% premium to Wednesday's close, and reported a third-quarter revenue and EBITDA beat; DoorDash rose about 7%.
The Bureau of Economic Analysis lists the advance Q3 GDP estimate and September personal income and outlays for 8:30 AM ET on Thursday.
body:
Several companies reported or announced deals before the Thursday open, and the group leaned positive even as megacap tech weakened.

Eli Lilly was the strongest large-cap earnings result. The Zepbound and Mounjaro maker posted adjusted earnings of $7.48 per share, well above the $6.26 consensus cited by LSEG, and revenue of $24.4 billion against $22.61 billion expected. Yahoo Finance reported the shares were up about 4.5% in premarket trading.

Norwegian Cruise Line also beat on both lines. Adjusted earnings were $1.12 a share against a consensus of 93 cents per FactSet, and revenue was $2.95 billion versus $2.88 billion expected. The stock jumped about 13% premarket, according to Yahoo Finance.

DoorDash said it will buy Instacart's parent, Maplebear, for $65 a share, an 11% premium to Maplebear's Wednesday close, in a $17 billion cash-and-stock transaction reported by Investopedia. DoorDash also reported third-quarter revenue and EBITDA above expectations, and its shares rose about 7%. Maplebear was little changed after trading resumed.

The macro calendar is led by the advance estimate of third-quarter GDP at 8:30 AM ET, released alongside September personal income and outlays by the Bureau of Economic Analysis. Those figures land a day after the Fed held rates and as traders weigh a possible December increase. Amazon reports after the close.

Not every name was positive. Investopedia reported that ServiceNow fell about 19% after its results and that Caterpillar was down about 9% premarket, which pulled Dow futures lower. Marvell Technology fell about 11% after a Bloomberg report that it is in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum Holdings, whose shares rose about 5.5%.

Energy was also in the mix. WTI crude futures slipped 0.9% to about $102 a barrel and Brent slipped 0.8% to about $114.40, after The Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance had sent a letter to Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei to try to restart peace negotiations, per Investopedia.

Intel also reports after the close, and Investopedia said options pricing implied a move of up to about 8% by the end of the week. Together with Amazon, the two reports will give the market more reads on AI demand and chip spending after the Alphabet selloff.

marketImpact.summary: Healthcare and consumer earnings are providing support, but the 8:30 AM GDP and inflation data could reset rate expectations. Deal-driven moves in DoorDash and Maplebear are company-specific and do not change the broader outlook.
